summary: Ana Agud is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied at the University of Salamanca (~1965–1970) and the University of Tübingen (~1970–1974), later serving as Professor in Salamanca's Department of Classical and Indo-European Philology (attested 2009).

Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Anagarika Dharmapala studied at Sri Jayawardenepura Maha Vidyalaya, St. Benedict's College, S. Thomas' College (~1876–1878), and Royal College (~1878–1883). He founded the Maha Bodhi Society (1891) and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

Active in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, Anagarika Govinda studied at Naples, Cagliari, and Freiburg, as well as under traditional teachers. He founded the Arya Maitreya Mandala and taught at Visva-Bharati, Patna, Allahabad, Lucknow, and Banaras Hindu University.

Anagarika Munindra worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Mahasi Sayadaw (1957–1966) and Satya Narayan Goenka, and served as superintendent at the Mahabodhi Temple from 1953 to 1957.
Anam Thubten Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche and held a teaching post at the Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies.

Ananda Guruge specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from the University of Peradeniya and University of London. He held posts at the National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration, California State University, Fullerton, and University of the West.

Working in Indology, history, archaeology, and philosophy, Ananda K. Coomaraswamy studied at Wycliffe College, University College London, and under Caroline Rhys Davids. He directed Ceylon's Geological Survey (~1903–1906) and held curator and research posts at Boston's Museum of Fine Arts.

Anant Sadashiv Altekar was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. He served as department head at Banaras Hindu University (~1930–1949), university professor at Patna University (~1949–1959), and director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (~1954–1959).

Anantalal Thakur was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as a professor at Mithila Sanskrit Research Institute (attested 1969) and as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.

Specializing in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, Anantanand Rambachan studied at the University of the West Indies, under Swami Dayananda Saraswati (~1976–1978), and at the University of Leeds (~1981–1984). He served as professor of religion at St. Olaf College (~1985–2021).

Andrea Acri is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Raffaele Torella, Arlo Griffiths, and Willem van der Molen, completing a PhD at Leiden University (~2006–2011), and was appointed maître de conférences at EPHE in 2016.

Andrea R. Jain works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University (PhD 2010), later holding faculty positions at Indiana University, including full professor in 2021.
Andrea Schlosser is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed both a Master's degree (by 2008) and a PhD (by 2014) at the Free University of Berlin.

Andreas Doctor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Leslie S. Kawamura at the University of Calgary, where he earned a PhD, and studied under traditional teachers Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche, Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche, and Phakchok Rinpoche.

Andreas Spengel was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Munich (~1856–1860) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1860–1863), and he later taught Albert Grünwedel.

Andree Dominique Messent specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Messent completed a PhD at the University of Bristol under supervisor Paul Williams, also studying under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.
Andrew B. Irvine works in philosophy and religious studies. Irvine earned a PhD from Boston University and served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College (attested 2009).
Andrew Garrett is a linguistics scholar who studied at Harvard University (~1984–1990). He has held a post at the University of California, Berkeley since approximately 1995.

Andrew Glass is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Washington (MA 2000, PhD 2006 under Richard Salomon), alongside teachers Mark Allon, Ulrich Pagel, Sonam Wanggyal, and Gudrun Melzer.

Andrew Goudie is a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Dean Close School and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1964–1970), and served as a professor at the University of Oxford from 1970 to 2014.
